title: INDIA Bloc to March in Delhi on October 12, Submit Memorandum to Chief Justice
excerpt: A day after meeting President Murmu to demand the CEC's resignation, opposition leaders announced a Delhi march and a memorandum to CJI Surya Kant, with Congress ordering all MPs to stay in the capital.
body:
• The opposition INDIA bloc will hold a protest march through Delhi on Monday, October 12, against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over its "vote chori" allegation.
  • Senior opposition leaders will meet Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and submit a memorandum seeking his intervention; Rahul Gandhi said the bloc wants "all options available" on the table.
  • The announcement follows the bloc's meeting with President Droupadi Murmu, where it demanded Kumar's resignation and the repeal of all Assembly elections held in the last two years.
  • Congress has asked all its MPs to remain in Delhi on Monday; police detained about 1,000 people during Saturday's protest at Jantar Mantar, ANI reported.

The opposition INDIA bloc will march through the national capital on Monday against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over its allegation of "vote chori," and a delegation of its senior leaders will submit a memorandum to Chief Justice of India Surya Kant seeking his intervention, Congress leaders announced on Sunday.

"On Monday, the Congress and the entire INDIA bloc and the country's youth will again take to the streets in massive numbers," Congress leader Rahul Gandhi said, adding that the bloc would also meet the CJI to press its case. "We will also meet the Chief Justice and demand that when the Constitution is being torn to shreds on Delhi's streets and democracy is being crushed, the guardians of the law cannot sit with blindfolds on."

Congress general secretary (organisation) K.C. Venugopal said the party appeals to every Indian concerned about democracy's survival to join the "massive" protest march against the nationwide vote theft it says is being orchestrated by the Modi-Shah regime. "Gyanesh must go. There will be no backing down," he added.

Context & Background

The announcement came a day after INDIA bloc leaders met President Droupadi Murmu and raised the "vote chori" claim to demand Kumar's resignation and the repeal of all Assembly polls held in the last two years. After the meeting, Gandhi said he was "shocked" that the president did not deny the election-theft charge.

https://x.com/PTI_News/status/2108998408312942816

The Opposition has been on the streets since Tuesday, October 6, when it first marched from Parliament to the Election Commission's office but was stopped on the way, with Gandhi staging an eight-hour sit-in inside the Akashvani Bhawan complex. On October 7 and 8, Opposition MPs staged marches to Jantar Mantar and then to Rajghat, alleging that Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Home Minister Amit Shah and the CEC had "hijacked the country through a criminal conspiracy of vote chori."

The aggressive push follows a report in The Indian Express that highlighted internal differences in the poll body, with Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi objecting on record at least 14 times in the last 10 months, including on the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. Last week, the INDIA bloc finalized a joint action plan on the SIR row, including rallies and "save democracy" marches. The Congress party has asked all its MPs to remain present in Delhi on Monday.

Impact & Analysis

Saturday's precursor protests showed how high the temperature has run: police detained approximately 1,000 people during a protest led by the Cockroach Janta Party at Jantar Mantar, including AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal, Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee and CPI(M) leader Pinarayi Vijayan, according to ANI. Authorities closed gates at 45 Metro stations, erected barricades at the Ghazipur border and suspended internet services in parts of the city. Gandhi has accused Delhi Police of "thuggery" and of allowing BJP workers to attack protesters, and separately the Supreme Court Bar Association has urged the CJI to intervene over the detention of lawyers near the Supreme Court on October 10 — a complaint that adds legal-community weight to the Opposition's push for judicial engagement.

"When the Constitution is being torn to shreds on Delhi's streets and democracy is being crushed, the guardians of the law cannot sit with blindfolds on."

— Rahul Gandhi, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha

Diaspora Angle

Electoral-integrity battles are followed closely by the Indian diaspora, which treats the credibility of home-country institutions as a measure of India's democratic standing. The Special Intensive Revision at the heart of the row — including in Bihar — is personal for emigrant families whose relatives' names sit on the rolls under review.

What's Next

All eyes are on Monday: whether the police permit the march's route, how large the turnout is, and whether the CJI meets the delegation and what he says. The opposition has also promised to submit evidence to the President, who asked for it at Saturday's meeting. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge is hosting INDIA bloc MPs for dinner on Monday evening, a signal the alliance intends to keep its ranks together through the week.
